title: Which technique to reach for
lede: Start from the symptom. Each question routes to the technique (and its section number) that addresses it; most real systems end up combining three or four.
caption: A decision flow for picking a context-management technique. Questions descend on the left; a "yes" routes to the technique on the right. Foundations come first because every other technique assumes you know your model’s real effective window and have caching on.

nodes.text: Context is filling up, costs are rising, or quality drops mid-task
Do you know the model’s real effective window, and is prompt caching on?
Measure first: RULER-style probes, context-rot curves; enable cache_control / implicit caching
Must knowledge survive across sessions, users or agents?
Add a memory layer: memory files (CLAUDE.md), Letta/mem0-style stores, graph memory
Is one session’s own history the bloat?
Prune cheap stuff first (old tool results, thinking blocks), then auto-compact the rest at a threshold
Are big documents, tool outputs or a codebase the bloat?
Load just-in-time: RAG / agentic search / repo map; offload raw outputs to files and keep pointers
Are independent sub-tasks competing for one window?
Isolate: sub-agents with their own windows that return condensed results; state schemas for big objects
Is the prompt itself long and repeated (prefix, few-shot, retrieved text)?
Lay out a stable, append-only cached prefix; compress retrieved text with LLMLingua-style tools
Window is healthy: keep utilization low (~40–60%) and re-check each release
